articles.title: Sabalenka crashes out of season-ending WTA Finals after losing to Svitolina
articles.summary: World number two Sabalenka’s season came to a disappointing end after she failed to reach the WTA Finals semifinals.
articles.body:
Elina Svitolina overwhelmed Aryna Sabalenka in the deciding set to seal a ⁠6-3, 3-6, 6-1 upset on Friday and reach the semifinals of the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells, where she will face Linda Noskova.

Svitolina absorbed and redirected Sabalenka’s power effectively, breaking the ⁠Belarusian six times before sealing her first victory over her opponent in more than six years with a forehand winner on her fourth match point.

With the win, Svitolina improved to 2-6 against Sabalenka in their career meetings.

“It was a bit of a roller-coaster match,” Svitolina told reporters.

“I played well in ‌the first set but lost a little bit of rhythm. She played well in the second and served much better. I was really happy with the way I could come back in the third after losing the first game.”

The Ukrainian again did not shake hands with Sabalenka after the match, maintaining her policy of not doing so with Russian and Belarusian players following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine .

Svitolina, the 2018 WTA Finals champion, will face Noskova on ⁠Saturday for a place in the final.

The defeat ended Sabalenka’s season ⁠on a disappointing note.

The second seed won Brisbane International in January and then Indian Wells and the Miami Open in March to complete the “Sunshine Double” but did not claim another title after that.

Sabalenka also surrendered the world number one ⁠ranking to Elena Rybakina at the US Open.

She had entered the season finale among the favourites after Rybakina withdrew on the eve of ⁠the tournament because of illness.

Sabalenka declined to speak to the ⁠media following Friday’s loss.

Earlier in the day, tournament debutant Andreeva continued her impressive run with a 6-2, 6-1 win over fellow Russian Diana Shnaider, her third straight-sets victory of the week.

Shnaider, Andreeva’s friend and doubles partner, replaced Karolina Muchova, who ‌withdrew before the final day of round-robin matches with a gastrointestinal illness.

Andreeva had already secured her place in the semifinals before facing Shnaider and will meet American Jessica Pegula on Saturday.

The eight-day, $10m ‌tournament was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells Tennis Garden due to the United States-Israeli war on Iran . The event will be played in Charlotte starting next year.

articles.title: Alcaraz y su raqueta sin cordaje: "Es el tipo de trabajo que me ha hecho entender y mejorar en pista indoor"
articles.standfirst: El murciano intenta impactar la pelota en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacando la mano hacia delante
articles.summary: El murciano intenta impactar la pelota en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacando la mano hacia delante
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, un innovador en los entrenamientos (Mirra Andreeva confesó que le copia ejercicios en el gimnasio), empezó a trabajar con una raqueta sin cordaje en su vuelta a los entrenamientos tras la lesión en la muñeca derecha. Carlitos, totalmente recuperado ya de la dolencia que le tuvo cuatro meses y medio alejado de las pistas, explica las razones que le llevan a seguir utilizando su Babolat sin cuerdas en el inicio de sus sesiones preparatorias. "Son ejercicios para tocarla o intentar tocarla en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacar la mano hacia delante. Es que aquí la pelota va muy rápida y tienes muy poco tiempo de margen. Si tú intentas jugar como en tierra. de tirar la pelota por arriba, al final te están comiendo. Y estos ejercicios son para intentar sacar la mano hacia delante, para tocarla siempre en el centro de la raqueta, para estar agachado, que aquí la bola no bota tanto. Es el tipo de trabajo que me ha hecho entender y mejorar en pista indoor", reflexiona el campeón de siete grandes. A Carlitos se le vio con una raqueta sin cordaje el pasado miércoles en la primera práctica realizada en el Inalpi Arena de Turín junto a su entrenador Samuel López.

images.caption: La secuencia del movimiento de Alcaraz sin raqueta. Joan Solsona

articles.title: Taylor Fritz makes honest admission after winning his first indoor title in Stockholm
articles.summary: Taylor Fritz captured the first indoor title of his career after winning the Stockholm Open on Saturday. The American star, ranked 10th in the world...
articles.body:
Taylor Fritz captured the first indoor title of his career after winning the Stockholm Open on Saturday.

The American star, ranked 10th in the world currently, beat Thiago Agustin Tirante in the final of the ATP 250 event. Fritz was in cruise control in the first set, which he won 6-2, but the Argentine rallied to force a third set and took his opponent to a tiebreak.

Fritz won the shootout 7-3 to triumph 6-2, 4-6, 7-6 and claim his 12th ATP title, ending his 2026 season on a high.

Taylor Fritz reacts after winning the Stockholm Open

"It was a stressful match for sure," said Fritz in his on-court interview after the win. "I felt like I came out, I was playing really well, and then I let some opportunities slip in the second set, and then he played a good game, a really good defensive game.

"I made a couple of mistakes. He's got a big serve; he was playing well. It kind of changed the momentum of the match. I was having a really hard time breaking him after that, and it turned into a really tight war of a match."

Reacting to winning his first indoor title, Fritz said: "It feels nice. I think I've lost a lot of indoor finals, but at the same time I didn't really look too much into it because when I won Tokyo the one year, the whole tournament was pretty much played indoors, so I do kind of half feel like I've had one. But it's good to get that one; now all that's left is a clay title."

Fritz's victory comes after a disappointing end to his Paris Masters campaign, where he came close to beating eventual champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinals, but came up short. That loss also put an end to his pursuit of ATP Finals qualification.

"It's really big for me to deal with what I dealt with in Paris," said Fritz. "I wanted to go home so bad; I think anyone would. But I knew that I would feel like a quitter and be a little disappointed in myself if I did that, so I'm glad I came here and made the most of it. I'm playing great tennis, and I get to end the year with a title."

This year marked the first time in three years that Fritz has failed to qualify for the ATP Finals.

articles.title: Alcaraz y Ferrero vuelven a abrazarse en público y en privado 361 días después
articles.standfirst: Los dos no coincidían desde el 18 de noviembre de 2025 cuando se despidieron en el hotel de Bolonia
articles.summary: Los dos no coincidían desde el 18 de noviembre de 2025 cuando se despidieron en el hotel de Bolonia
articles.body: Cuando el 18 de noviembre de 2025, Carlos Alcaraz y Juan Carlos Ferrero se despidieron en el Royal Hotel Carlton de Bolonia poco podían imaginar que no volverían a abrazarse hasta este sábado en Turín, en un entrenamiento previo al inicio de las ATP Finals. Juan Carlos acompañó entonces a Carlitos a la localidad italiana, sede de la fase final de la Copa Davis. El jugador de El Palmar no pudo defender a España en la máxima competición por países a causa de un edema en el isquiotibial. Los dos estuvieron juntos en las pruebas médicas que Carlos se realizó en un hospital de la capital de la región Emilia-Romaña y cenaron después con el resto de los miembros de la selección nacional. "Va a ser un poco raro tras tanto tiempo, le voy a dar un abrazo", reconocía el murciano en su comparecencia pública del viernes tras hacerse la foto oficial junto al resto de participantes. Habían pasado 361 días desde que Alcaraz y Ferrero no cruzaban sus miradas. El primer momento se produjo al mediodía, lejos de las cámaras, según ha podido saber MARCA. Los dos se encontraron comiendo en el restaurante de 1.200 metros cuadrados que ha montado Red Bull para los tenistas y que se asemeja a los de la Fórmula Uno. El segundo abrazo se produjo en la pista central del Inalpi Arena porque Carlitos se saltó el calentamiento previo de una hora para preservar su físico tras los problemas de estómago del viernes. Apareció con una aparatosa rodillera. Juanki estaba allí junto a su nuevo pupilo, el estadounidense Ben Shelton. Se dio un tercer abrazo con Carlitos a la conclusión de la sesión preparatoria. Fue incluso más largo que los dos anteriores. Ambos trabajaron durante siete campañas y el preparador llevó al murciano a ganar seis grandes y ser el número 1 más joven de la historia. Ferrero permanecerá hasta el lunes en la capital de la región del Piamonte por lo que tendrá tiempo de ver en directo el debut de Shelton este domingo frente a Arthur Fils. Posteriormente, viajará a Asia donde tenía unos compromisos adquiridos antes de unirse profesionalmente a Shelton a finales de octubre. Su primer torneo oficial al lado del jugador estadounidense será el Open de Australia (17 al 31). Allí también estará Carlitos, que acudirá a la defensa de la corona de campeón.

images.caption: Alcaraz luce una rodillera. Joan Solsona
El mensaje de bienvenida de Carlitos a Juanki.

articles.title: Current world No. 1 Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend over domestic abuse allegations ahead of ATP finals
articles.summary: World No. 1 Alexander Zverev is facing a civil lawsuit from former partner Brenda Patea regarding domestic abuse allegations, challenging his claims of innocence just before the ATP Finals.
articles.body: Alexander Zverev will begin his bid for a third ATP Finals title under renewed legal scrutiny after his former partner, Brenda Patea, filed a civil lawsuit over his public statements about the domestic abuse case she brought against him. The action, lodged in Berlin, challenges his claims that the allegations were disproved and that his innocence had been established, despite the earlier proceedings ending without a verdict.Brenda Patea sues Alexander Zverev over claims his innocence was provenThe lawsuit was filed on September 18, with Patea, the mother of Zverev’s five-year-old daughter, seeking legal action over comments the German tennis player made after criminal proceedings relating to her allegations were discontinued in June 2024.The case centres on Zverev’s repeated assertions that the allegations had been proven false and that his innocence had been established. Patea argues that those statements misrepresented the outcome of the proceedings and breached an agreement reached when the original case was settled.According to tennis journalist Ben Rothenberg, who first reported the new action for Bounces, Patea’s legal representatives had previously written to Zverev asking him to stop making such statements. The lawsuit says that he did not respond. Her lawyer, Michael Scheele, said the action was intended both to seek redress for his client and to prevent further statements of the same nature.“This lawsuit serves both to provide satisfaction to the plaintiff and to prevent further infringements,” Scheele said.He argued that Zverev’s comments had caused particular harm because they were made to an international publication and subsequently repeated by German media.“In the present case, a serious infringement has occurred,” Scheele said. “The defendant made a false factual assertion to an international newspaper that his innocence had been proven. This statement was disseminated internationally and picked up by numerous German media outlets.“It discredits the plaintiff as a liar and portrays her as a person who wrongfully accused the defendant. Furthermore, the defendant has breached a contractual obligation to refrain from such conduct, which makes the motive and degree of his fault particularly egregious.”The lawsuit seeks compensation for damage to Patea’s public standing, alongside an injunction intended to prevent further statements. She had initially applied for a preliminary injunction, but withdrew that application on September 14 before filing the claim four days later.The Berlin court has assigned the case a number and issued a procedural order dated November 5. However, the lawsuit had not yet been formally served on Zverev at the time of the reports. The action therefore represents a new civil dispute over his public comments, rather than a reopening of the criminal proceedings that ended in 2024.The lawsuit also sets out why Patea had previously hesitated to pursue Zverev through the courts. It says she feared reprisals from him and anticipated that he would be less willing to reach an out-of-court agreement over the child support she was seeking.Why Alexander Zverev’s original domestic abuse case ended without a verdictThe dispute stems from allegations made by Patea about an incident in Berlin in May 2020. She accused Zverev of pushing her against a wall and strangling her with both hands during an argument. Patea had made her allegations public, and Zverev has consistently denied them.On October 2, 2023, Berlin’s Tiergarten district court issued a penalty order against the tennis player, imposing a €450,000 fine. The amount was calculated through 90 daily payments of €5,000. Zverev challenged the order, preventing it from becoming final and leading to a criminal trial in 2024.Proceedings began in May that year, while Zverev was competing at the French Open, where he reached the final. The case was discontinued in June after an agreement was reached between Zverev, Patea and the prosecution.Under the settlement, Zverev agreed to pay €200,000, comprising €150,000 to the state and €50,000 to charitable organisations. Crucially, the proceedings ended without a finding of guilt or innocence, and Zverev did not admit to the allegations.The distinction became central to the statements that have now prompted Patea’s civil action. After the proceedings were discontinued, Zverev suggested during a press conference at Roland Garros that the decision itself demonstrated his innocence.“They’re not going to drop the case if you’re guilty at the end of the day. I don’t know what translations you have, but that’s what it means. Done. We move on. I never ever want to hear another question about the subject again. That goes out to everybody,” he said.He returned to the subject in a June 2025 interview with L’Équipe, conducted the morning after winning his maiden Grand Slam title at the French Open. Asked about the allegations by journalist Quentin Moynet, Zverev challenged the premise of the question.“First of all, this isn’t that kind of interview. Secondly, you know that the accusations have been proven false?” he said.When the journalist argued that the allegations remained a legitimate subject of discussion, Zverev added: “I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.”Patea’s new lawsuit challenges precisely that interpretation of the outcome. The criminal proceedings were discontinued following a settlement, but there was no trial verdict establishing that the allegations were false or that Zverev had been cleared.Zverev faces renewed scrutiny as he prepares for ATP FinalsThe lawsuit arrives at a significant moment in Zverev’s career. The German has risen to world No. 1 and secured the year-end top ranking for 2026, and is preparing to compete at the ATP Finals in Turin, where the tournament begins on Sunday. He will be seeking a third title at the season-ending championship.The new legal action is not the first time Zverev has faced allegations of abuse involving a former partner. Olya Sharypova, another former girlfriend and a former tennis player, made allegations against him in October 2020, describing incidents of alleged physical and emotional abuse during their relationship in 2019. She said some of the incidents occurred in cities where ATP tournaments were being held.Zverev denied Sharypova’s allegations. The ATP opened an investigation that lasted 15 months before announcing in January 2023 that it would take no disciplinary action, citing insufficient evidence to substantiate the claims.That investigation was separate from the criminal proceedings brought by Patea in Germany. The ATP’s decision concerned whether there was sufficient evidence for disciplinary action under its own rules; the Berlin case involved allegations examined through the German criminal justice system.Zverev has denied the allegations made by both women. The new lawsuit does not establish liability, and its claims will have to be considered through the civil proceedings. It does, however, bring his public account of the Patea case back into focus just as he prepares for one of the biggest tournaments of his season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
